text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Syrian newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Syrian President Hafez al-Assad discusses with Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi difficulties of the peace process and confirms: "Syria wants peace and demands the implementation of the Madrid priciples."
- Prodi stresses the significance of commitment to previous peace agreements and praises Syrian-Italian ties.

- Israeli government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu threatens to force Palestinian President Yasser Arafat out of Gaza and warns Palestinians ahead of breaking the ground for Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
- Tourism minister says Syria now has the capability to accomodate three million tourists.

- State-owned Syrian textile companies have inventory worth 2.5 billion Syrian pounds. Directors admit quality of production is not good and costs are high. Syria invested around 2.3 billion pounds in 1996 to improve production.
- Syrian wheat production in 1995-1996 fell to three million tonnes from around 3.3 million tonnes in previous harvest. Estimated 1996-1997 production is around four million tonnes.
- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak says Syria will not resume peace talks until after Israel's commitment to full withdrawal from the Golan Heights.
- Syrian head of People's Assembly (parliament) Abdel-Qadir Qaddoura receives a letter from Sudanese counterpart Hassan al-Turabi over the war situation in Sudan.
- Industrial establishments increased the amount of exported goods to dollars 68.6 million in 1996 from dollars 65.3 million in 1995.
- State-owned establishment for post and telecommunication's 1996 turnover was 9.6 billion pounds, profit was 6.4 billion pounds and investment's expenditure was 3.5 billion.
(U.S. dollar = 50 pounds in the black market)
